questions.text: An electron is released from rest near an infinite non-conducting sheet of uniform charge density ' $-\sigma$ '. The rate of change of de-Broglie wave length associated with the electron varies inversely as $\mathrm{n}^{\text {th }}$ power of time. The numerical value of n is $\_\_\_\_$ .

steps:
Let the momentum of $\mathrm{e}^{-}$at any time t is p and its de-broglie wavelength is $\lambda$.
Then, $\mathrm{p}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\lambda}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{dp}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{-\mathrm{h}}{\lambda^{2}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
\mathrm{ma}=\mathrm{F}=-\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\lambda} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \quad\left[\mathrm{~m}=\text { mass of } \mathrm{e}^{-}\right]
\end{array}$$

Where, -ve sign represents decrease in $\lambda$ with time
$$\mathrm{ma}=\frac{-\mathrm{h}}{(\mathrm{~h} / \mathrm{p})^{2}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{p}^{2}}{\mathrm{mh}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
\mathrm{a}=-\frac{\mathrm{mv}^{2}}{\mathrm{~h}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
\frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{\mathrm{ah}}{\mathrm{mv}^{2}}
\end{array}$$
here, $\mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{qE}}{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}} \frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_{0}}$
$$\mathrm{a}=\frac{\sigma \mathrm{e}}{2 \mathrm{~m} \varepsilon_{0}}$$
and $\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{u}+\mathrm{at}$
$$\mathrm{v}=\mathrm{at}$$

Substituting values of a \& v in equation (1)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\frac{2 \mathrm{~h} \varepsilon_{0}}{\sigma \mathrm{et}^{2}} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{~d} \lambda}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^{2}} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=2
\end{array}$$
